feature: One way to add, colour and remove any part of a shape
summary: Everything a layer paints is now one list called Appearance: Fill, Outline and Shadow, each with a tick that switches it on or off, the colour it paints, and its own settings folding open underneath. A rectangle's outline can be taken off, which was impossible before.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. The flag is next-shape-parts, on by default. A rectangle's panel goes from four sections to three: the Rectangle section and the Shadow section are gone.

try.do: Draw a rectangle. Look at the Appearance section: three rows, three ticks.
Untick Outline. The ring goes, and the row keeps only its name and its tick.
Tick it again, then click the chevron at the end of the Outline row to open Width.
Tick Shadow and open it. The outline's Width folds away as the shadow's five sliders open.
Press Cmd-Z twice and watch the shadow and then the outline come back.
Drop a screenshot on the canvas and tick its Outline: the same row, the same Width.
Draw an arrow. Its one colour is called Color and has no tick, because an arrow with no line is nothing.

evaluate: Reading Fill, Outline, Shadow down one column, is it obvious that they are the same kind of thing?
Is a tick the right control for switching a part on, or did the shadow's old switch read better?
Does folding the outline away when you open the shadow ever cost you something, or does the shorter panel win?
Appearance is the new name for what used to be Color. Does that heading say what is under it?
Corner Radius stayed under Effects rather than moving in with the outline. Is that where you look for it?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every picture here is a real capture of the window, not an offscreen render.
Take an outline off, save, reopen, and switching it back on gives you a 4pt line rather than the width you had. The width is remembered by the window, not the file. Undo restores it exactly.
Taking an outline off does not arm the tool the way emptying a fill does, so the next rectangle you draw still comes out with one. Worth deciding which behaviour you want.
Pick a rectangle and a screenshot together and you get two rows both called Outline, one for each kind of ring, each saying which layers it reaches. One row cannot yet paint both.

Against the model in docs/design/shape-parts.md, Corner Radius did not move into the shape's own section as the report asked: it is one row that also rounds screenshots, frames and groups, and those have no shape section to move it to.
